title: `rollback` command that cannot remove existing commands or user data
question_or_target: Implement rollback to a previous version from the rollback manifest such that commands, skills, and user data introduced OUTSIDE the rolled-back version survive. The seeded failure class is 'rollback removes existing commands or user data'; the rollback must compute a set difference, not restore a snapshot wholesale.
answer: Set-difference rollback at tools/plugin/rollback.py restores only owned_to paths from the target payload and unlinks only owned_from − owned_to. Live paths outside owned_from are foreign and are never unlinked or overwritten (clash refuses). A throwaway HOME rehearsal kept commands/user-created.md byte-identical. An independent payload-derived hash census matched the post-rollback tree (v1 ∪ foreign). Wholesale snapshot restore deleted all three foreign paths, so the preservation test discriminates. Rollback-then-reinstall returned the original hash census. SUCCESS:IMP-0026
